column1: Considering the challenges facing the ACME Group through the increasing competitive pressure, with increasing customer and regulatory requirements, we need to continuously increase our efficiency in the Product Development Process in order to stay competitive
column2: RFI_SE ver1.0 final

column1: Looking at our current engineering practices, that are very much hardware component driven, we want to be more pro-active (up-front system design).
column2: RFI_SE ver1.0 final

column1: Furthermore, the ever increasing complexity of our products makes it necessary to always improve our current engineering practices where needed, for instance to have better control of our Product Families.
column2: RFI_SE ver1.0 final

column1: Since we have a commitment to efficiently develop and offer superior products exceeding our customers’ expectations, upfront development and Systems Engineering is a key mechanism, see Figure 1.
column2: RFI_SE ver1.0 final

column1: In this RFI, the following fields of Systems Engineering expertise will be in focus: Stakeholder Requirements Management, Requirements Management, Systems Architecture and Design (MBSE), Requirements driven Verification and Validation.

column1: However, surrounding fields of expertise, e.g. Systems Analysis and general support processes (e.g. report & measurements, Configuration Management), is also of interest.

column1: The next step for ACME is to start practicing Model Based Systems Engineering, MBSE.

column1: Systems Engineering within ACME is today very requirements driven but now it is time to start looking at MBSE with support of standard general-purpose modeling language (e.g. SysML, UML and IDEF).

column1: Among such guidelines it is included the technical standarization of these resources, through a hierachical model of architectures similar to that used by NATO, as an instrument of coherence and technical integrity.
